sentences.text:
Amanullah Khan, aged about 35 years, son of Md. Idris Khan, resident of Village- Azad Basti,
Mandu, P.O. & P.S. Mandu, District- Ramgarh (Jharkhand). ... ... Appellant Versus The State of
Jharkhand ... ... Respondent

---------
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay Hon'Ble Mr. Justice
Pradeep Kumar Srivastava

For the Appellant : Mr. Nilesh Kumar, Advocate For the Respondent : Mr. Abhay Kumar Tiwari,
A.P.P. For the Informant : Mr. A.K. Rashidi, Advocate.

th 04/Dated: 05 January, 2026 I.A. No. 14423 of 2025
1.

Heard Mr. Nilesh Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P assisted by Mr. A.K.
Rashidi, learned counsel appearing for the informant.

2.  This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during pendency of this appeal.
3.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 504 and 506 the I.P.C. and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years along with fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C.
4.
It has been alleged that on the assurance of marriage, the appellant had committed rape upon the informant.

5. Submission has been advanced by learned counsel for the appellant that though in the first information report, it was indicated by the informant that on the pretext of marriage physical relationship was established by the appellant with her, but in her evidence as P.W.3 she has given a Amanullah Khan vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140563813/
1 different version to the effect that it was the appellant who had forcibly taken her on the roof and committed rape upon her on Page | 1 several occasions.

entities.text: Amanullah Khan vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that the appellant was all along on bail during trial.
6. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel appearing for the informant has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

Learned counsel for the informant has submitted that the learned trial court has considered each and every aspect of the matter and in fact the evidence of P.W.3 who is the victim categorically reveals the manner in which she was subjected to rape by the appellant.
7. It does appear that the version of the victim has undergone a sea change in her evidence as P.W.3.
It further appears from the medical report that there was no external or internal injury found on the private part of the victim.
It also appears from the evidence of the other witnesses including the mother of the informant that there was an affair going on between the appellant and the victim.
8. On consideration of the aforesaid facts, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of Learned District & Additional Sessions Judge-I, Ramgarh in Sessions Trial Case No.
69 of 2021 arising out of Mandu P.S. Case No. 89 of 2021 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 593 of 2021.
9. Accordingly, I.A. No. 14423 of 2025 is disposed of.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Date:- 05th January, 2026.
